description: Per-character ordered bundle of CharacterCaptureDataTable row IDs, used to select the capture configuration appropriate to each UI capture context.

ID.simple: Row key, normally the character ID that Character::Id_CharacterCapture points to.
ID.technical: FName primary key (ImportKeyField=Id in the export). FindCharacterCaptureRow reads Character::Id_CharacterCapture and calls FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_CharacterCaptureSet> on each table in CharacterCaptureSetDataTables (DTM +0x430), stopping at the first hit. A None id on the Character row means no set is resolved.

Id_CharacterCapture.simple: Ordered list of CharacterCapture row IDs for this character's capture contexts.
Id_CharacterCapture.technical: TArray<FName>, 8 slots in every exported row (commonly six populated context-specific IDs followed by None padding). The capture actor iterates the list in order; encountering a None entry returns no capture, otherwise each ID is resolved via FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_CharacterCapture> across CharacterCaptureDataTables (DTM +0x440) and the first row whose CaptureType equals the requested slot type is returned. A missing capture row also ends the walk. The array order therefore controls both search order and the early-abort behaviour on padding.

notes: Export contains 45 rows, each with exactly eight Id_CharacterCapture slots; populated prefixes in the sample data are <character>_CHARACTER_SELECT, _STORYCHARACTER_SELECT, _VS_ALLY, _VS_ENEMY, _FREE_BATTLE and _CUSTOMIZE, followed by None padding.

The join is Character::Id_CharacterCapture -> CharacterCaptureSet row -> CharacterCapture row filtered by capture type; the result feeds asset loading, spawning and montage playback in AGameCharacterCaptureActor.
There is a single retail table registered as 'CharacterCaptureSetDataTable' and loaded into DTM +0x430; no numbered shards are present in the export.
Reconstructed source with retail RVA comments; no claim about Blueprint-only consumers or uncooked content.

usages.detail: FindCharacterCaptureRow resolves the set using Character::Id_CharacterCapture.
Iterates Id_CharacterCapture, stopping on None or a missing character-capture row.
Returns the first capture row whose CaptureType matches the slot.
